full_judgment: 9. The plaintiff-respondent examined 4 witnesses in support of his case and filed documents which were marked Exhibit-1 to Exhibit-7 and the same were admitted without objection. The defendant-appellants as well examined 4 witnesses and produced Exhibit-A to Exhibit-C. The defendant though objected before the trial Court to the effect that the Suresh Chandra Chowdhury had no son named Sanker Prashad Chowdhury but has obtain exparte decree in the Title Suit No. 202 o 1969 that they had no absolute right, interest and possession in the suit land and the trial Court has held that there is evident that Suresh Chandra Chowdhury had a so named Sanker Prashad Chowdhury and has been possessing the suit land. The trial Court also decreed the suit holding that on 06.09.1972 the defendants have dispossessed the plaintiff from the Schedule land. The fact of Sanker Prasha Chwodhury being a son of Suresh Chandra Chowdhury has been proved by PW-1 {Exhibit-1,2,3,3(a)}. The fact to the alleged dispossession the plaintiff has sought to prove that the plaintiff was dispossessed on 06.09.1972 from the Schedule-3 land of the suit. Fact remain that though the defendant claims the sin land but they have not challenged the decree in Title Suit No. 202 of 1969 at the proceeding in Execution No. 5 of 1970. On the contrary the defendant No.1 ha failed to prove the alleged patta, kabala deed dated 03.06.1972 and unregister bainanama dated 10.04.1969 being the basis of his alleged possession and title the suit land and thus failed to prove the same.
